utterances.text: Was this dirt road, as you were travelling south from Vera to Pacetin, was that dirt road to the left or the right of the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That road was as you go from Bobota, Pacetin, and Vera on the left-hand side of the road. It was between the roads leads from Bobota and to Pacetin, and the road that is marked by number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I've never served in the military, I've never been in combat. I've never under been artillery or mortar fire, and nor I do imagine most people -- have most people in this room. But can you help us understand why it would be safer to travel on a dirt road to the left of that highway than it would be to just travel down the highway?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, let me correct you. It was not a highway. It was just an asphalt road with just one drive way split in two so that the vehicles could travel in both directions. But there were just two lanes. It was safer because fire was never opened on any of the dirt roads. From Nustar, fire was opened from howitzers, mortars, and a tank. The tank shell has a very high start velocity and travels in a straight line, whereas mortar shells fall under a certain angle of descent. They follow a certain arch as their trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What does that have to do with making it safer to travel along the dirt road than on the regular road, the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has a lot to do with that, because in our units, there were topographic maps of the area, and it was easy to identify the co-ordinates of the asphalt roads. For anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm done with that document, Mr. President, but I would tender it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D62, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, yesterday at page 5474, you were describing the meeting between Mr. Hadzic, Mr. Radovan Stojicic, and your commander, Mr. Sljukic at Mr. Hadzic's house in Pacetin. And at page 5406 of your testimony, which was earlier in the day, you said that you could not see their interaction. Now, am I correct that you did not see either the first meeting that you say was at Mr. Hadzic's house or the second meeting, which you then say was at the Pacetin local commune? Is what you said about not seeing the interaction, is that true for both meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And how long did they remain, these three individuals whom you identified being at Mr. Hadzic's house, how long did they remain there before they went to the local commune?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how much time they stayed there, but I would say that they were not there long.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you witness them leave the house, Mr. Hadzic's house?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw my superior as he was leaving and as he came to my car. I didn't see when Mr. Goran Hadzic left the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Are you saying that Mr. Hadzic remained behind and your commander, Mr. Sljukic, left the house and went to the local commune on his own, or was he perhaps accompanied by Mr. Radovan Stojicic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My superior was the first to leave the house. He came to the car and then he told me where to -- where I should drive him. I drove him there. He went into that building. I remained behind in the car with the escorts who were in the car with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And while you were sitting in that car, how far were you from the -- from the local commune building at that point?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I was about 20 or 30 metres away from the entrance into that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And please tell us everything that you observed while you were sitting there observing the local commune building.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Various people entered the building. Civilians, people in uniforms. They went in and out. And that's all I could observe as I was sitting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, who did you identify as arriving and entering the building?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one point in time, some minutes after my commander and I arrived, Lieutenant-Colonel Vaskovic arrived. Mr. Stevo Pavkovic also arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some other people arrived. They went into the building. They came out. I stopped paying attention. There were a lot of people whom I didn't know and whom I had never seen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you see Radovan Stojicic enter the building?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him. However, when I returned to the base, my commander, Zeljko Sljukic, told us that he had attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I think I heard you say that you left with your commander before Radovan Stojicic did. Let me start that question again. I thought I heard you testify that you saw -- or that your commander left Mr. Hadzic's house before Mr. Stojicic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when you left in the car from Mr. Hadzic's house to go to the local commune, did you drive directly there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So if Mr. Stojicic had gone to the local commune and he departed after you did with your commander, wouldn't you have seen him enter the local commune building?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't pay that much attention to the people who were entering and leaving the building. And as for the exact moment when Radovan Stojicic arrived, I wasn't focused on that. Perhaps I was parking the car at that moment, or perhaps I was involved in a conversation with the people who were in the car who were on Mr. Sljukic's escort detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Hadzic enter the local commune while you were parked there in front of it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You just testified that Mr. Sljukic, your commander, told you that he -- that Radovan Stojicic participated in the meeting. Did your commander tell you whether Mr. Hadzic was at that second meeting or did he not mention that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't mention Mr. Goran Hadzic. He said that Radovan Stojicic, Badza, had attended as well as Mr. Savo Milovanovic, who was the commander of the defence of Brsadin village. My commander, Sljukic, very often met with the latter and had a lot of contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And did Mr. Sljukic or anyone else tell you about what had transpired at either of the two meetings, either the first one at Mr. Hadzic's house or the second one at the local commune?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in general terms, he told me that they discussed further activities by the units that were deployed there and co-operation among those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Anything more specific than that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nothing more specific was mentioned. He said that they had agreed future co-operation, future combat activities, future supply of the units that were deployed in the area, and the organisation of the local authorities in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we please have P2027, please. And if we could please go to page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, this is your statement coming up on the screen in front of us. It's paragraph 44. And you have it there in the B/C/S in front of you. And your entire description of your trip to Pacetin and the meetings -- the meeting that occurred there is as follows: "I attended a meeting between Radovan Stojicic, Badza, my commander, Zarko Sljukic, Lieutenant-Colonel Vaskovic, Goran Hadzic, Rade Leskovac, Savo Milovanovic, Major-General Bratic, Mile Jerkovic, Arkan's logistics commander, and several other men. The meeting was held in the house of Goran Hadzic in Pacetin village. At this meeting, Bratic proposed a plan for liberating ... Brsadin silo, but Radovan Stojicic, Badza, was against that plan and proposed another one, upon which the JNA and we acted." Now you'll agree with me, Mr. Kovacevic, that this is quite a different description than the one that you've given in this courtroom towards the end of yesterday and today; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you have just read out and the persons that I've mentioned in paragraph 44, that meeting was not in Pacetin. That meeting took place in Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Why does it say "the meeting was held in the house of Goran Hadzic in Pacetin village"? Why does it say that at paragraph 44 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When -- I've just told you that the meeting which was attended by Mile Jerkovic and General Bratic took place in Dalj. That's what I said. And the persons who you just mentioned were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, we're going to discuss the alleged meeting in Dalj which you describe at paragraphs 45 and 46 of your statement. What we see in paragraph 44 is a different meeting which you say in your statement which you, on oath, have sworn to yesterday morning, you say that there's a meeting in Pacetin with these individuals. Don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have stated that the first meeting was in Pacetin and that Mr. Radovan Stojicic, Badza, attended it, as well as Mr. Rade Leskovac. And I stated that, according to my commander, that meeting was to discuss combat activities that were supposed to be carried out, the supply of the units deployed in the area, and the organisation of the civilian authorities in the area under our control.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you've given -- and that's a different version of events than the one that appears in paragraph 44 of your statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The subsequent events and my deployment in the area together with my commander --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Kovacevic. I think you can answer my question with a yes or a no. Is it correct, yes or no, paragraph 44 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is stated under 44 is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So it's correct that there was a meeting with all of these individuals at Mr. Hadzic's house in Pacetin?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot claim that all the persons that are mentioned here were in Mr. Goran Hadzic's house in Pacetin. However, from subsequent conversations, from my subsequent deployment in the area, and my subsequent conversations with my commander, those persons are -- were at the meeting in the Territorial Defence Staff in Pacetin village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that you have not in your testimony here mentioned the presence of several of the individuals mentioned in paragraph 44. You haven't mentioned that there were two meetings. You haven't mentioned that there was a plan developed at that meeting for an attack on Brsadin silo. You have not mentioned that you concluded from this event that Radovan Stojicic had de facto control over the territory of Eastern Slavonia. You haven't mentioned any of those things. Now, at page 5700 of yesterday's transcript you were asked the question by the Prosecution whether you would give the same testimony in court as appears in your statement. You clearly haven't done so, have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If I could just interject there. In the question he says that there's no mention in the witness's testimony of two meetings, and the witness had clarified that there were two meetings. I'm not sure if my learned colleague is referring to two meetings in Pacetin or one meeting in Pacetin and one meeting in Dalj, so perhaps it would help to clarify that before putting the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Would you clarify, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You have not mentioned that there were two meetings in Pacetin. You have not mentioned that any meeting attended by Mr. Hadzic was also attended by Mr. Stojicic and your commander, Mr. Sljukic. You have not mentioned that the topic of the meeting, according to you, was a plan to attack Brsadin silo. You have not mentioned the conclusion that you drew about Badza in relation to that meeting. You have also not mentioned the names of some of the individuals whom you identify in paragraph 44 as having appeared at either of the two meetings or having been mentioned to you as attending either of the two meetings. Now, I think the matter is clearly put to you. And I think it's a simple question I ask you at that point. That's different. The testimony you've given here before the -- Their Honours, under oath, is different from what appears in paragraph 44; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that I first took my commander to Goran Hadzic's house. He went into the house. After a certain while, we left and we drove to the local commune building in Pacetin. According to what I know, that's where the centre of the Territorial Defence of Pacetin village was. The second meeting was held there, and that meeting, as far as I can remember, lasted between three and four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 1D437, please, which is Defence tab 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And before I ask my question in relation to this document, let me just ask you: When you were asked yesterday morning by the Prosecution that you would testify in the same way or that you would give the same answers as you had given in your statement, did you understand, Mr. Kovacevic, that you were entitled to answer no if you didn't remember things that were in your statement. Did you understand that if you no longer remembered things that were in your statement, you were entitled to answer no?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my first statement. I provided it in 2003, when my recollection was much fresher. However, whatever I said then, whatever I stated then, I stick by that. At the trials of Stanisic and Simatovic and Mr. Perisic, some more details were provided with regard to the paragraphs in my statement. A lot more details were asked for. And as for some details, for example, the duration of the meeting and certain other things, I really can't remember. I can't be precise about some of those things. If I was in one location, I really can't remember, as I sit here today, where that location was. If I was there only once. As for the other locations where I spent a longer time, I can still remember them. I can mark them on the map. I can mark the exact distance between certain locations, how many kilometres were they away from each other. I can also mark the road that we took from the Vera village to Brsadin village. It was a dirt road. I can mark that road. I can tell you what features we crossed on our way. And so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you -- you're now saying that indeed you can't remember certain details such as the duration of the meetings and certain other things. Would you agree that that includes you can't remember in some respects, and certainly this is the case in respect of paragraph 44, you can't remember the individuals who were present? You can't remember whether this was one or two -- well, now you've given a different account, two meetings instead of one, and you've forgotten the purpose of the meeting as expressed in your statement. Would you agree with me - and I think you have gone part way down this road - would you agree with me that you've forgotten those other details that I've mentioned in paragraph 44?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I forgot certain details, but as for the more important people who were at that meeting and whom I saw with my own eyes and those I heard from my commander were there, I cannot forget or omit these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we turn the page of the document in front of us to paragraph 7. This is a proofing note that we received from the Prosecution. I presume that you have not seen this document. Am I correct? It's only in English.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, there, at the first sentence of paragraph 7 it says: "In relation to paragraph 44 of his statement, he," and this is referring to you, Mr. Kovacevic, "he stated that there was an initial gathering at the house of Goran Hadzic in Pacetin and then a meeting at the agricultural centre, which was located in the centre of town." Now, was that second meeting at the commune or was it at the agricultural centre, as this proofing note appears to indicate?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A meeting was also held in the building of the local commune. To the best of my knowledge, in that building, there were offices of the agricultural co-operative.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: When did you provide this information to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the interview, during the proofing when we were going through this. I think it was on the 10th of May, 2013, if my memory serves me right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You mean it was a month ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Just to interject there. There was an earlier version of the proofing note that we provided to the Defence I believe a couple of weeks ago, which is also contained in this more full proofing note. So there were two meetings, just in fairness to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I don't think there was any need for that intervention, Mr. President. It was a simple question of when did he provide that information to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, but the witness wouldn't be aware of the process of producing proofing notes, and so I wanted to avoid any confusion in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So was that -- am I correct in understanding your answer, that that was about a month ago that you provided that information?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I had a discussion with the Prosecution on the 10th of May in Belgrade. Then I also spoke to the Prosecution once I arrived here in The Hague. Now what is the exact provenance of this note, when it was drafted, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we can go back now, please, to your statement, which is P2027. And, again, going to page 10, which is paragraph 44, you mention a name here which you've also mentioned at least twice in your testimony here, and that's Savo Milovanovic. Are you sure that that's the name of the TO commander in Brsadin?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You're sure that his name wasn't Savo Milankovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, all the times that we went to see Mr. Savo in Brsadin, because my commander was co-operating closely with him concerning also supplies to the observation post, I remember his last name as Milanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yesterday at page 40 -- 5465, you mentioned the TO commander of Bijelo Brdo, what was his name? Can you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajko Pantelinac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Are you sure it wasn't Caslav Niksic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, to the extent we co-operated and all the times we went there, Mr. Rajko Pantelinac had his own unit in Bijelo Brdo and co-operated with my commander, and later in 1993 or perhaps 1994, he was also president of Dalj municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: For the record, the name that I mentioned was Caslav Niksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Who was the TO commander in Pacetin?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent very little time in Pacetin so I don't know who the commander was. I mean, commander of the defence in Pacetin. And I did not mention in any of my statements that I knew who the commander of defence in Pacetin was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 04642, please. Prosecution tab 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, it's not true that you've never identified the TO commander in Pacetin. Do you know that that's not true?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember ever stating the name of the defence commander in Pacetin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we please have transcript page 6708.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: At page 6708, and it's coming up on the screen, at line 16 -- well, starting at line 14. This is the question: "Q. Witness, you state here that -- or, rather, tell us first do you know who Goran Hadzic was? "A. Goran Hadzic was from the village of Pacetin. Initially he was commander of the defence of the village of Pacetin." Do you remember giving that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember saying that Mr. Goran Hadzic was earlier on the commander of Pacetin defence. But later on, when I arrived, I don't know who held that position. And that Mr. Goran Hadzic used to be the defence commander is something I found out from my superiors.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, you've said here today that there was a second meeting, or a different meeting, which you say Mr. Hadzic attended in Dalj. Can you please describe that meeting for us.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in my statement that second meeting was held at the Municipal Assembly of Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you said at 5407 that you thought it was in the second half of October. Can you give us any further details or description as to this meeting. Who was there, anything you learned about it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that meeting there was my superior, Mr. Zarko Sljukic, Lieutenant-Colonel Vaskovic. From what I learned, the meeting was also attended by the commanding cadre of the Novi Sad Corps; also Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, with his deputies in his unit; and also Mr. Goran Hadzic; Mr. Radovan Stojicic, Badza, as well. Because as we arrived Dalj, and my commander got out of the car, I saw Mr. Goran Hadzic standing outside the municipal assembly building shaking hands with some people and talking to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was Milorad Ulemek there, also known as Legija?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my commander, Zarko Sljukic, I heard that Mr. Milorad Ulemek, known as Legija, later also attended that meeting. At what point he joined the Serb Volunteer Guard, I don't know, but I only heard from my commander that he was also at that meeting. And I also heard from him that this gentleman held the position of deputy commander of the Serbian Volunteer Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: When you say that later -- when you use the word "later" in saying that Legija attended the meeting, do I understand you to mean that he arrived part way through the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not inside the building. I was not at the meeting. I was outside in the street with the other men from the entourage of my commander. So when exactly Legija arrived at the meeting, I don't know. I can't say anything. I know only what I heard from my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that's what he told you, that Milorad Ulemek came part way through the meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said that Legija appeared a bit later. Now when exactly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But later at the meeting, not after the meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, this has been asked and answered twice now. He said he arrived later. When exactly Legija arrived at the meeting, I don't know. That's at transcript page 68, line 23. So I don't know if it's going to take us much further to keep repeating the same question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I have not foreclosed of the witness the possibility that he arrived after the meeting. There's a forensic purpose for this that is coming up very quick, very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So he didn't arrive after the meeting, he arrived during the meeting. Maybe a little bit late, but during the meeting according to your commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he came to the meeting, according to what my commander said. Now whether he was just late for the meeting, or arrived after the meeting, I can't tell you exactly. I told you already, my commander told me that Mr. Ulemek came to the meeting, and he was at the meeting. Now whether he arrived after the meeting, or into the meeting part way, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 0642, please. The same document we just had up. And we're going to go back to the same page in fact, which is 6708 at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now I'll start reading while that is coming up for your benefit, Mr. Kovacevic. And this was your testimony in the Stanisic case. And here's the question. And to be clear, this is referring to paragraph 45 of -- of your statement, the statement that has been admitted in this case. "Q. Which year does this portion of your statement relate to? Is it 1991 when you arrived in the area of Erdut?"

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And for the benefit of the the Registry, now we're turning over to page 4709.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "A. Yes. "Q. You said ... you recall there being Goran Hadzic, Arkan with his commander [sic] including Milorad Ulemek, also known as Legija, his deputy at the time; is that right? "A. Yes. "Q. This was a meeting held sometime in 1992 in a place called Dalj. Did you see Legija in 1991? "A. No, not in 1991. In 1992 when the meeting in Dalj took place. "Q. You had not seen Legija at all before the [sic] meeting? That meeting? "A. No, not Legija. I would see Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, his deputy commander for logistics, Mr. Mirko Jerkovic. "Q. Do you recall which month this meeting was held? "A. I can't recall that. The only thing I know was that it was held in the building of the Dalj Municipal Assembly." Now, to be fair to you, sir, there appears to have been a question that might not quite get the year correct, but did you mean to testify there in that case that you think that this meeting occurred in 1992? Do I read your testimony correctly in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in 1991, and that meeting was held in October 1991 in Dalj, I did not see Mr. Milorad Ulemek, Legija, at that meeting myself. What I said was that, from talking to my superiors, I learned that Mr. Ulemek, Legija, attended that meeting, arriving late. And in 1992, I saw Mr. Milorad Ulemek, Legija, in the field in Western Srem, Slavonia, and Baranja. In my statement and in the transcript, the name of the deputy commander for logistics is misstated. It's Mile Jerkovic, not Mirko.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, let me just focus your attention on line 7 to 9. The question was: "This was a meeting held sometime in 1992 in a place called Dalj. Did you see Legija in 1991?" Your answer: "No, not in 1991. In 1992 when the meeting in Dalj took place." Aren't you saying there that this meeting that's being discussed occurs in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Again, this has just been asked and answered. It's the same question that was just asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Overruled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that in 1991 at that October meeting in Dalj, I did not see Mr. Milorad Ulemek, Legija, myself. Instead, I found out from my commander that Legija was at that meeting. I have been saying this for the umpteenth time today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I kindly ask how much time I have left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] You mean in total or you don't mean today? You mean time left for your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Some 40 minutes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, am I correct that you witnessed an altercation between Mr. Vaskovic and Arkan sometime in September or October 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when was that and what did you see?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said in my statement, a problem cropped up between one officer of the Serbian Volunteer Guard and the commander of the Ruma Artillery Battalion, Lieutenant-Colonel Vaskovic. We went to the training centre in Erdut where the Serbian Volunteer Guards were based, and he wanted to iron out some misunderstandings with Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And those misunderstandings, in summary, concerned Mr. Vaskovic saying that he would prevent and arrest some of the Serbian Volunteer Guard whom he considered were committing crimes. Does that accurately sum up the nature of the altercation?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the gist of the misunderstanding was that. But there was also a problem of mistreatment of JNA members, namely, members of the Ruma Artillery Battalion, who went on a two-, three-day leave home, and transport was organised from Vera village to Ruma, and Serbian Volunteer Guards searched them on the bridge and confiscating -- confiscated certain things from them. And, at the same time, Mr. Vaskovic wanted to put a stop to some looting they were guilty of. And he said that he would take certain steps to stop it if they attempt to go on in the area where he has control.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Those last words are what I'm particularly interested in. Do I understand correctly that Mr. Vaskovic was concerned about this because the crimes were occurring within his area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, do you see the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Oh, I didn't understand that we were breaking at 2.00, but -- I'm not sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I thought everyone was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm sure that I was told, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The plan is to have a one-hour lunch break and resume at 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness. Mr. Kovacevic, the court usher will escort you out of the court for the lunch break for one hour, and you will be back at 3.00, hopefully to finish your testimony for the -- for today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned. --- Luncheon recess taken at 2.01 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: While the witness is brought in, a short oral ruling, if possible. The Prosecution filed today a motion for extension of time to submit additional documentation demonstrating that Witnesses GH-079 and GH-142 are unavailable pursuant to Rule 92 quater. The Defence see that motion and can take a position on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: A response as is in the process or has been filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. And would you object to the motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We do oppose the motion, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a look at it then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sorry, in relation to that motion, if I could just quickly add that as an update, we have received today the medical documentation in relation to, I believe, it's GH-079, and so we can provide that today. That was one of the witnesses for whom we were requesting extra time. So we can just provide that update.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gosnell, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, going back to the meeting that you describe as having been attended by the commanding cadre of the 12th Corps, amongst other individuals in Dalj, you say that that meeting occurred at what you describe at the Municipal Assembly building; is that correct? Is that how you know that building where they met?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the name under which I remember that building. Later on, I learned that the government was based in that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Which government?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, that was the government of the -- Slavonia, Western Baranja, and Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you describe this building.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building was located in the centre of Dalj. It was on the right-hand side as you arrived in Dalj from Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is it possible you're confusing the commune offices with whatever offices of the district government, or the proto-district government might have existed in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the structure of that organisation before the war -- actually, I don't know whether Dalj was a municipality before the war or was it just a local commune? During the SAO Baranja and Western Srem district, the village of Dalj certainly became a municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, sir, I -- I didn't use the expression "municipality." It was you who did that in your testimony in the Stanisic case in 2010; for the record, at page 6709. And that was were you used the expression "Dalj Municipal Assembly." So even in 2010, am I right you knew that building as the Dalj Municipal Assembly building?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You didn't attend that meeting yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know specifically what, if anything, was decided at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from my conversation with my commander, I know that the meeting was organised, to -- to discuss the final operations to liberate Vukovar. In that conversation, my commander, Sljukic, stated something about Goran Hadzic. What he said was that Mr. Goran Hadzic is a very promising man and that he always advocated a peaceful situation of the -- a peaceful solution of the situation in the area. He always insisted on the population in the area to be protected, especially the Serbian population, which was threatened by the then-Republic of Croatia. And he also told me about Mr. Goran Hadzic, that Mr. Goran Hadzic advocated the protection of all the population and that he tried, according to my commander, to find a peaceful solution to the situation and that Goran Hadzic also discussed the political situation and the combat activities, but that he did not have -- enjoy political support. The political situation was different than the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Am I right in thinking that if a command order was going to be given for the final assault on Vukovar, it would be somebody from the command cadre of the 12th Corps who would make that final decision and issue that final order? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, judging by the situation in the area during that period of time, it was the 12th Corps and the Serbian Volunteer Guards that were deployed there, and on the Sid and Tovarnik side there was a guards unit. Judging by the hierarchy of the then-Yugoslav People's Army, the General Staff of that army was probably supposed to issue an order to the 12th Corps and the Guards Brigade. As for the further orders and activities, those were in the hands of the 12th Corps and the guards unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: During your testimony yesterday at page 5443, you were talking about who has check-points around the Bogojevo bridge and what you say there is: "It was the military police and the Serbian Volunteer Guard that controlled the bridge on the Croatian side." Now, during what period was that the case, that it was the military police and the Serbian Volunteer Guard that controlled the bridge on the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I noticed that, I moved around the area before Vukovar was liberated, and that was in the end of August until the fall of Vukovar, and when Vukovar fell, I returned to Belgrade via Tovarnik and Sid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So what date range specifically? What dates do you say that is the case?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be precise. I can't tell you on what dates. But, in any case, that was from August 1991, when I was there, when I crossed the bridge into Serbia. In other words, that was from August 1991 until the liberation of Vukovar. That's when I was there. I don't know who controlled the bridge after November 1991. I never crossed the Bogojevo bridge after that, so I was not abreast of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when you say it was the military police and the Serbian Volunteer Guard, do you mean that they were present at the same time together at a check-point?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the Croatian side, there were both the military police of the Novi Sad Corps and members of the Serbian Volunteer Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was that a yes to my question? They were together at a check-point?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have D41, please, which is Defence tab 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, did you need a pass from the JNA in order to drive around in the area of Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A pass to move around the area was not needed. We had travel orders from the unit that was deployed there, and that document depicted the military post number and a gas station where we were supplied with fuel. And when we crossed from Croatia into Serbia, if we needed to go there, then we had to have a pass which showed the route, the registration plate of the vehicle, and if we carried arms, we were not allowed to carry long-barrelled arms across the bridge. The only thing that we could carry was our personal weapon, i.e., a pistol, and that pass also depicted the registration number of that pistol, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I see we don't have the document in e-court, but I'm just going to skip to the next topic. Mr. Kovacevic, at paragraph 4 of your statement, and we can bring that up, please, at P2027, you indicate that you -- well, there it is. In any event, I'm just going to proceed, Mr. President. At paragraph 4 of your statement, which is at P2027, you indicate that you had been - and this is the statement you gave in 2003 - that you had been under investigation for a traffic accident. "In 1998 I was charged and convicted, but the appeals court overturned this conviction. Other than that, I have never been under investigation." That was in 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sorry, are we going to get the statement on the monitor, in accordance with the prior ruling from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I have no objection to it being pulled up. That's why I gave the reference. And it's page 2, paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now when you were asked questions by the Prosecution yesterday, you indicated that that wasn't true. And we're going into that a little more. But I want to, first of all, ask you whose idea was it that paragraph 4 should appear in your statement? Did you raise that with the people interviewing you, or did they ask the question of you and then you responded?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, that question was put to me by those who interviewed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you know that it was -- that this paragraph 4, at the time did you know that that was false?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that was an official conviction. As for that paragraph, there was some other cases which were in the stage of investigation. They were not completed by then, which is what I stated yesterday when I was asked about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, yesterday you didn't answer the question I've just posed, and you again have not answered it. The question is: Did you know that paragraph 4 was false when you signed this statement in 2003?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of that. However, those convictions were not final. Actually, the cases had not been heard before the court by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But the issue isn't whether or not you had been convicted. The issue is the second sentence or, excuse me, the third sentence. You don't say, Other than that, I have never been convicted. You say, Other than that, I have never been under investigation. Now you knew that to be false at that time, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Then why did you tell that falsehood to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, under law, a person who is not found guilty is presumed to be innocent, until that person is found guilty and convicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And in 2009, when you testified in the Perisic case, by which time you had been investigated in numerous cases, and you had been convicted in at least four cases, you swore that this statement in front of us, including paragraph 4, not only that it was correct but that you would answer that the same way again; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I provided this statement in 2003. I repeated that in the Perisic case and again in the Stanisic/Simatovic case. I stated that, in the meantime, I was convicted. In 2003, I was under investigation, and until the conviction became final, that person was presumed to be innocent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's take a look at just a few of these court documents concerning the proceedings against you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 02532, please, Defence tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: To briefly summarise, this is a judgement which appears to be an appeals judgement from the Subotica Municipal Court, and the cause of action appears to arise from you promising to obtain ten tonnes of cement, you received 1450 Deutschemarks in exchange for providing it this, and not only did you provide the cement as requested and these details all appear at page 10 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I see we have the wrong document. Let me restate the number. 02532. This looks promising. Now if we can please turn to page -- well, just first look at page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It says there in the very first paragraph that there had been a public hearing held on 18 November in the presence of the prosecutor and the accused. Now am I correct - and let's just limit ourselves to this question - did you take part in a hearing in a criminal case against you on the 18th of October, 2002? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th of October, 2003, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It says 2002, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was in 2002. There was conviction but it was not final. All of the convictions were made public, and a single sentence was issued and here this is just one conviction. When the single sentence was made public on all convictions, some of the convictions were overturned and a single sentence was passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, sir, I don't think a single one of these convictions were overturned. There was a joinder of sentences but that's a different issue. In any event, let's take it step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 10 of this document, please, in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it describes that you have received 1450 Deutschemarks in exchange for ten tonnes of cement. You did not supply the amount. And, in addition, you did not return the money. And the court says --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm afraid that's not the correct page in English. Could we go back one page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Here in the large paragraph in the middle of the page, it says: "Added to this the fact that the defendant changed his statement several times about the reasons why he failed to carry out his obligation towards the injured party. The logical conclusion is that at the time when the defendant promised to deliver the cement to the injured party he knew that he would not fulfil his obligation within the deadline." Is that correct, you knew that you weren't going to fulfil this obligation but you, nevertheless, took the money and made the promise?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that I would not be able to fulfil my obligation. The situation when the delivery of the cement was agreed was different. That happened after the bombardment of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Later on, the complete manufacture of cement and building materials were placed under the authority of the agency for the reconstruction of the land, which is why I could not fulfil the obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This document is tendered, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D63, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 02554, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, this involves a promise on your part to procure a car, an Audi, in fact, from Germany, for which you received the sum of 800 euros. This is a judgement in the case from the Municipal Court in Ruma.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we could please turn to page 5 in the English. And, for the record, the date of this is the 19th of February, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page it says: "Based on all of the above, the court finds that the actions of the accused bear all the [sic] subjective and objective elements of the crime of fraud ... during the trial it was established beyond any doubt that the accused ... had misled the injured party, telling her that his brother could get hold of a cheap vehicle and he persuaded her to give him 800 euros to her own detriment. And after she handed over this amount, he kept deceiving her that he would bring her the vehicle he promised, but during the trial it was established that he had not obtained this vehicle, since his brother, to whom he referred when coming to an agreement with the injured party ... did not know anything about this agreement." Did you defraud this lady of 800 euros on the false promise of providing her with a car?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I took 800 euro from the lady. I could not obtain the car. After the trial, the lady in question was reimbursed. She received the money back after the court issued the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You only gave her, her money back when the court had issued an order to you to do so?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The lady filed a complaint because she didn't want to wait any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That document is tendered, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D64, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 02553, please. Defence tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is from the Subotica District Court dated the 11th of February, 2004, entitled: "Judgement." You're named there as the accused. Down there at sub-point b on page 1: "The District Court regarding as proper the prison sentence as set out in the aforesaid judgement for the crimes of which Milomir Kovacevic was pronounced guilty in that judgement, namely ..." And then the crimes listed are: Unauthorised procuring and bearing of a fire-arm, fraud, forging documents, and apparently the separate crime of forgery. Is that right, that were convicted of these various offences, fraud, forging documents, and forgery?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an integrated -- amalgamated sentence for the -- under the previous two judgements you've shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You're denying that this involves a separate course of conduct on your part, involving weapons and forging the documents that supposedly would entitle you to carry and hold those weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not denying that. I'm just saying that these weapons were not used. What happened is that during a brawl, the weapons just fell out of the holster that I was carrying. The weapons were not used in that brawl.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This document is tendered, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D65, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 1D436, please. Defence tab 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document from the Office of the National Council for Co-operation with the ICTY, dated the 12th of May, 2009. The information recorded in this document is that you have been investigated no less than eight times, or at least under eight separate dossiers, and you appear to have been convicted in four separate judgements. Is that accurate, that that's -- do you have knowledge that that was the number of investigations and convictions against you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, there were some investigations. Some investigations were suspended, and the rest that resulted in prosecutions, were eventually combined into a single sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What was that single sentence; and how much time did you actually serve?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That single sentence was four years, and I served three.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What years did that occur, that you served that sentence?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was sometime after 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: After you gave your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Immediately after?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not immediately after.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This document is tendered, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D66, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Where was your father while you were in Eastern Slavonia, serving in Vera? Where was your father at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My father was with the Yugoslav People's Army in the area of Eastern Slavonia and Baranja, until the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Where precisely was he? Who was he serving with?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army, the Ruma Artillery Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is the unit that's led by Mr. Vaskovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: What was his job?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while, my father was driver to Lieutenant-Colonel Vaskovic, and the rest of the time, until the 10th of October, he was a gunner. He was a gunner because that was his military evidentiary specialty in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just two more questions, Mr. President. I know I'm probably over time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The first question, sir, is: Did your father ever drive Mr. Sljukic? You've identified him as the man that you've driven for. Did your father ever drive him?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My father drove Mr. Sljukic just as I sometimes drove Lieutenant-Colonel Vaskovic, as required.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you never, in all of your statements, testimony, proofing notes, supplement information sheets, deemed it germane to mention this?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't think it was necessary because my father left on the 10th of October and went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 1D437, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one clarification, Mr. Gosnell. Mr. Kovacevic, the 10th of October of what year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes, so could we please have 1D437. And if we could turn to page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kovacevic, again, this is the document that was given to us by the Office of the Prosecutor based on their interviews with you. Apparently two interviews. Or at least interviews at two different times. And I draw your attention to paragraph 11. And the language used there is this: "The witness said that the notes that he previously had kept concerning events set out in his testimony have now been destroyed." You'll see it doesn't say "lost." It says "destroyed." Did you tell the Prosecutors that those documents had been lost or that they had been destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I told the Prosecution the documents were lost. They were missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kovacevic. Mr. President those are my questions. I do have a number of documents to tender at this point. In particular, I would like to tender the three sets of documents. One is the testimony from the Stanisic case. The other is the August supplementary information sheet which was signed by the witness. That was prior to his testimony in the Stanisic case. And I would also like to tender the proofing note in this case. Now I -- we, of course, have been here before. Sometimes Your Honours have been willing to admit previous statements and sometimes you haven't. I would suggest, Mr. President, that this is an occasion when, in particular, the Stanisic testimony, should be admitted. And the reason why I would suggest that arises from the objection or at least the intervention that you heard from the Prosecution on Monday when they disputed, for example, that a reference to documents was in fact a reference to his notes. Now the only way to -- and Your Honour quite rightly said at the time, Well, we'll have a look at this and determine whether or not that's clear based on the entire context of what is written there. And Your Honours won't really be able to make a final determination about that unless you have those pages of transcript, and I'd suggest that that's a -- that's a recurring conundrum for Your Honours. There were many things that were put to the witness which, if you take one word out of place, you could say, Well, that's not impeachment material. But then when you look at two or three pages you will see that indeed the meaning is clear. At least that is our submission and the Prosecution will undoubtedly offer different submissions. But the only way for those submissions to make any sense for Your Honours is if you actually have the material. So our submission is that those materials should be admitted for the purpose of impeachment only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Yeah. First up, I'm not sure if we should address this now or should I finish re-examination. I only had two clarifying questions. And then get into the legal questions. I'm in your hands, either way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's -- that's a good suggestion, Mr. Gillett. Then after your re-direct and eventually the Judges' question we can excuse the witness and discuss this matter further eventually. So your questions in re-direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, just two questions in re-direct. Firstly, during cross-examination, at transcript page 5453, you were describing the chain of command, and you referred to the field mission in Western Srem and Baranja. Did you mean to restrict your answer to just Western Srem and Baranja or does it also include other areas?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- that concerned only Western Srem and Baranja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you understand those areas to cover also the area in which the towns of Dalj and Erdut are located, for example?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Western Srem and Baranja cover the area from the Hungarian border via Beli Manastir, Bijelo Brdo, Kopacki Rit, Erdut, village Vera, Pacetin, Principovac farm, Bobota, Bogdanovci, Marinovci, Brsadin, Vukovar, and up to Tovarnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Okay. I think that clearly answers the question. At that same portion of transcript, you continued on to explain - and this was this relation to the chain of command - you said: "The situation was rather messy because, in addition to the Yugoslav People's Army, there was the Serbian Volunteer Guard of Mr. Zeljko Raznjatovic." However, you were then cut off in your explanation by the Defence. Can you recall what you were going to explain in relation to that question?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in response to that question, I was going to add the fact that under the constitution of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and under the laws, only the Territorial Defence and the Yugoslav People's Army were officially supposed to act without any paramilitaries. The Serbian Volunteers Guard was not a regular army from the SFRY, it was a paramilitary unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And that was the situation as it was supposed to occur under the rules and the constitution, according to your previous answer. But when you said "the situation was rather messy," does that mean that it was different from what was supposed to occur in theory or not?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, things occurred differently than they were supposed. There were cases when the Serbian Volunteer Guard took over certain operations and did so on their own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: No further questions on re-exam. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, this brings an end to your testimony. We thank you for coming to The Hague. You're now released as a witness, and we wish you a safe journey home. The court usher will escort you out of court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good-bye, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, I -- I said I would respond to the legal submissions just previously made, so I'm prepared to go through with that right now, if it pleases Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So perhaps if we start with the Stanisic/Simatovic transcripts which my learned colleague described, we did not object to the extension of time for cross-examination of this witness and it is extended to, I believe, four hours of cross-examination. We say that it's unnecessary for those transcripts in Stanisic and Simatovic to be tendered into evidence in this case because the key points have all been addressed during cross-examination and the key bits of transcript have been read into the record. Specifically in relation to the point where I challenged a certain issue during cross-examination, I have reviewed the transcripts, and, in fact, the question from the Stanisic and Simatovic transcript that I was concerned about was read into the record albeit in a prior question, and that's at transcript page 5466, lines 14 to 18. The witness was then able to answer the question. And that's at the same transcript page, lines 20 to 23. So that adequately deals with my objection. It's on the record in this case and we say it would be duplicative to then admit the transcripts again that have already been incorporated where relevant. Now, Your Honours in a previous decision have indicated that you prefer not to be overburdened with extraneous materials, prior testimony. In this case of Stanisic and Simatovic we're talking about four days of testimony and cross-examination, most of which goes to issues not involving the accused Goran Hadzic. I believe there's only one reference that I could see to Hadzic which has been read into the record and covered by questions, and this is covered at transcript pages 6708 to 6709 of the Stanisic and Simatovic transcript. And that -- that portion, if you look at our transcript, was read into the record. It concerned the dates of the meeting in Dalj and the presence of Milorad Ulemek, Legija. So on this basis, we would say that it's unnecessary to admit the Stanisic and Simatovic transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We will discuss this and come back to you probably tomorrow, and, if not, it will be a little bit later. Would you like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just one -- one small comment on the submissions that were made by my learned friend. Certainly not all the issues that are relevant to this witness's credibility were gone into. I used my four hours as efficiently as I could, but there simply were other issues concerning credibility that I did not go into and I couldn't gone into exhaustively without spending another three hours or four hours with the witness. I don't think that would have benefitted the Chamber very much. But nevertheless, I -- it should be clearly reflected there were issues I did not go into that are highly relevant to credibility, and those transcripts are not tendered in any way because they're relevant to Mr. Hadzic. It has nothing do with that. It has to do with the witness's credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gillett, about the -- your request for an extension of time for the 92 quater witnesses, you told us that you have a document now concerning 079. Is that -- is that the one?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I believe so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And are you -- is -- is that -- is that document in -- in Court's hands? Is it filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I can explain. We just received it this morning by fax. We have an investigator in the field who faxed that through, and so we are intending to file that with the Chamber along with the medical documentation for GH-083 as indicated in the motion for extension. So it would just leave, I think, it's GH-142 who we are still awaiting the Croatian authorities to provide the relevant document for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: But then my conclusion would be that your request for extension of time is still valid for both; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I thought the deadline was 11 June for the submission of these materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And when -- when is that? That's tomorrow, isn't it? Or today. Isn't it today? Yeah, it's today; right? Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. We've been -- this has been moving back and forth during the course of the proceedings. Documentation did come in from the field just today, and it's going to be submitted today to the Chamber, and this is in respect of GH-083 and GH-079 and we just are in the process of drafting a -- a document we're calling a supplement documentation for those. So with respect to GH-083 and 079, we are actually meeting the Chamber's deadline, which is today, June 11th, and so the motion for the extension of time would, in our submission, be then moot in respect of those two witnesses. And then the third witness is GH-142, and on that one we had been hoping to obtain a death certificate which has not yet received. And on that, our intention has been to file by way of a reply to the Defence response the Request for Assistance that was sent out to the Croatian authorities requesting the documentation because the Defence indicated that they felt that the initial motion didn't provide enough information about the efforts undertaken to obtain the documentation in a timely way. So we're going to be submitting the Request for Assistance so the Chamber and the Defence can see when that documentation was requested. However, we still have not obtained that documentation back in response to the Request for Assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Court adjourned.
